newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-KARRIE WEBB WINS LPGA TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP, MONEY TITLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-KARRIE WEBB WINS LPGA TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP, MONEY TITLE.

text.p: Sensational Australian Karrie Webb capped her first season on the LPGA Tour by becoming the first woman golfer to earn more than $1 million in a year Sunday when she won the $700,000 LPGA Tour Championship.

Webb's fourth victory of the year was worth $150,000, boosting her 1996 earnings to a record $1,004,000. She topped Britain's Laura Davies by more than $75,000 to become the first rookie to win the LPGA money title since Nancy Lopez in 1978.

The 21-year-old Webb was in the top 10 in almost every statistical category and led the Tour with 15 top-10 finishes in 25 events. The four wins tied her with Davies and Dottie Pepper for the LPGA lead.

She fired a seven-under-par 65 Sunday for a four-round total of 16-under 272 at the Desert Inn Golf Course. Webb started the day tied for the lead with Emilee Klein, a 22-year-old Californian who shot a three-under 69 and fell into a second-place tie with Kelly Robbins and Lopez at 12-under 276.
Robbins fired a 65, while Lopez -- still seeking her first win since 1993 -- shot 66.
Davies shot a 67 and settled for a fifth-place tie with Juli Inkster and Brandie Burton at 11-under 277. Davies already had secured LPGA Player of the Year honours.
